claim: Deep learning vision models that use data augmentation techniques that make non-geometric pixel-level manipulations (e.g., PixMix, AugMix) during training are robust to poisoning attacks with global triggers (e.g., manipulation of size > 95% of total image area - noise patterns, intensity/contrast manipulation) when up to 1% of the training data is poisoned.  A model is considered robust if the post-training attack success rate remains within 5% of a similar model trained using the same augmentation techniques but with only clean data.

experiment_recipes.goal: Verify that the CIFAR-10 poison budget and global-trigger geometry exactly match the claim before any model training
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Construct two predeclared global trigger families: fixed global noise pattern and global intensity/contrast manipulation. Pass only if the poisoned training subset contains exactly 500 of 50000 CIFAR-10 training images, i.e. 1% poison, and for every poisoned image the trigger mask or changed-pixel fraction covers >95% of spatial image area. Any poison count >500, any trigger covering <=95% area, or any label/trigger mismatch refutes that the experiment instantiates the claim constraints.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Backdoor and poisoning protocols first audit the attack budget and trigger mask because a robustness result is uninterpretable if the poison rate or trigger size differs from the claimed threat model.
experiment_recipes.label: norm_card_method

experiment_recipes.goal: Validate that the constructed 1% global-trigger poisons are a nontrivial backdoor attack under a standard matched-budget vision baseline
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train 0%-poison and 1%-poison ResNet-18 baselines using random crop + horizontal flip, for the fixed global noise trigger and the global intensity/contrast trigger, with the same target-label protocol used later. Compute delta_ASR = ASR_poisoned_triggered - ASR_unpoisoned_triggered on non-target CIFAR-10 test images. Pass only if each trigger family has delta_ASR > 5 percentage points for at least one predeclared target label while clean accuracy drop is <=5 percentage points. If not, the attack apparatus is too weak or not a stealthy poisoning/backdoor attack for the headline test.
depends_on: Verify that the CIFAR-10 poison budget and global-trigger geometry exactly match the claim before any model training
experiment_recipes.rationale: A matched standard-augmentation baseline is the conventional sanity check that the poison construction can actually create a backdoor at the stated 1% budget rather than merely failing because the attack is ineffective.
experiment_recipes.label: norm_card_method

experiment_recipes.goal: Directly test whether PixMix training is robust to 1% global-trigger poisoning on CIFAR-10
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train paired PixMix ResNet-18 models with 0% poison and with exactly 1% poison, using the validated >95%-area fixed global noise and global intensity/contrast triggers. For each predeclared target label and each trigger, compute ASR on triggered non-target test images. PixMix passes the claim only if ASR_poisoned is within +5 percentage points of ASR_unpoisoned for every trigger-target run and clean test accuracy of the poisoned model is within 5 percentage points of the corresponding 0%-poison PixMix model. Any trigger-target run with ASR_poisoned - ASR_unpoisoned >5 percentage points refutes the PixMix part of the claim.
depends_on: Verify that the CIFAR-10 poison budget and global-trigger geometry exactly match the claim before any model training
Validate that the constructed 1% global-trigger poisons are a nontrivial backdoor attack under a standard matched-budget vision baseline
experiment_recipes.rationale: This is the direct backdoor-poisoning evaluation of the named non-geometric pixel-level augmentation method under the exact poison budget, trigger area, and ASR threshold named in the claim.
experiment_recipes.label: norm_card_method

experiment_recipes.goal: Directly test whether AugMix training is robust to 1% global-trigger poisoning on CIFAR-10
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train paired AugMix ResNet-18 models with 0% poison and with exactly 1% poison, using the validated >95%-area fixed global noise and global intensity/contrast triggers. For each predeclared target label and each trigger, compute ASR on triggered non-target test images. AugMix passes the claim only if ASR_poisoned is within +5 percentage points of ASR_unpoisoned for every trigger-target run and clean test accuracy of the poisoned model is within 5 percentage points of the corresponding 0%-poison AugMix model. Any trigger-target run with ASR_poisoned - ASR_unpoisoned >5 percentage points refutes the AugMix part of the claim.
depends_on: Verify that the CIFAR-10 poison budget and global-trigger geometry exactly match the claim before any model training
Validate that the constructed 1% global-trigger poisons are a nontrivial backdoor attack under a standard matched-budget vision baseline
experiment_recipes.rationale: AugMix is separately named in the claim, so it requires its own direct matched-budget ASR test rather than being inferred from PixMix.
experiment_recipes.label: norm_card_method

experiment_recipes.goal: Check that PixMix robustness is not an artifact of testing only the single maximum poison rate or only a non-adaptive trigger insertion order
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Repeat PixMix training for poison rates 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1%, with the same >95%-area global noise and intensity/contrast triggers, and include an adaptive variant where the trigger is re-applied after the PixMix stochastic augmentation path during poisoned-sample training. Pass only if, for every poison rate <=1%, every trigger family, and every predeclared target label, ASR_poisoned - ASR_unpoisoned <=5 percentage points and clean accuracy drop <=5 percentage points. Any adaptive or lower-rate setting with delta_ASR >5 percentage points refutes the claim for PixMix.
depends_on: Directly test whether PixMix training is robust to 1% global-trigger poisoning on CIFAR-10
experiment_recipes.rationale: Poisoning robustness claims should be checked across the entire stated up-to-1% budget and against attacks adapted to the defense/augmentation pipeline, not only against a fixed non-adaptive construction.
experiment_recipes.label: norm_card_method

experiment_recipes.goal: Check that AugMix robustness is not an artifact of testing only the single maximum poison rate or only a non-adaptive trigger insertion order
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Repeat AugMix training for poison rates 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1%, with the same >95%-area global noise and intensity/contrast triggers, and include an adaptive variant where the trigger is re-applied after the AugMix stochastic augmentation path during poisoned-sample training. Pass only if, for every poison rate <=1%, every trigger family, and every predeclared target label, ASR_poisoned - ASR_unpoisoned <=5 percentage points and clean accuracy drop <=5 percentage points. Any adaptive or lower-rate setting with delta_ASR >5 percentage points refutes the claim for AugMix.
depends_on: Directly test whether AugMix training is robust to 1% global-trigger poisoning on CIFAR-10
experiment_recipes.rationale: This control tests the standard concern that strong data augmentation may only suppress a non-adaptive trigger placement, while an augmentation-aware poison can restore the backdoor within the same 1% and >95%-area threat model.
experiment_recipes.label: norm_card_method

baseline_recipes.goal: Verify that the poisoning budget and global-trigger definitions satisfy the claim before any training
baseline_recipes.method_under_test: Global-trigger poison-set construction for later PixMix and AugMix runs
baseline_recipes.attack_or_condition: Construct two target-label backdoor poison sets per target class: fixed full-image additive/blended noise pattern and global intensity/contrast transform. Poison exactly floor(0.01 * N_train) non-target training images and relabel them to the chosen target class. Construct triggered test sets by applying the same trigger to all non-target test images.
baseline_recipes.pass_condition: Pass only if poison_fraction <= 1.000% for every poison set and triggered_pixel_area_fraction > 95.0% for every poisoned training image and every triggered test image, where triggered_pixel_area_fraction is the fraction of pixels with absolute per-channel change > 1/255. Refute the setup if any trigger or poison set violates either numeric bound.
baseline_recipes.rationale: The claim only applies to attacks using no more than 1% poisoned training data and global triggers covering more than 95% of image area; this cheap check prevents testing a different threat model.
baseline_recipes.label: baseline

baseline_recipes.goal: Build clean PixMix and AugMix reference models whose clean-trigger ASR baselines are stable enough for a 5 percentage-point robustness comparison
baseline_recipes.model: WideResNet-28-10 or ResNet-18, same architecture for all conditions
baseline_recipes.method_under_test: Clean training with PixMix and clean training with AugMix
baseline_recipes.attack_or_condition: Train clean models with 0 poisoned samples using standard PixMix or AugMix training. Evaluate ASR on the globally triggered non-target test images from the gate recipe, even though no poison was used in training.
baseline_recipes.pass_condition: Pass only if the clean training set contains exactly 0 poisoned samples and, for each augmentation method and each global trigger, the maximum minus minimum clean-model ASR across at least 3 random seeds is <= 5 percentage points. Refute the apparatus if clean-reference ASR variation alone exceeds the claim's 5 percentage-point tolerance.
constraints_not_enforced: >95% area global trigger in poisoned training data
depends_on: Verify that the poisoning budget and global-trigger definitions satisfy the claim before any training
baseline_recipes.rationale: The claim defines robustness relative to a similar clean model trained with the same augmentation. If clean-reference ASR is unstable by more than 5 percentage points, the headline comparison is not decisive.
baseline_recipes.label: baseline

baseline_recipes.goal: Validate that the chosen 1% global-trigger poisoning attack is strong enough to measure robustness rather than merely failing by construction
baseline_recipes.model: Same architecture as headline, trained without PixMix or AugMix; use only standard crop/flip or no augmentation
baseline_recipes.attack_or_condition: Train clean and 1%-poisoned non-PixMix/non-AugMix models using the same poison sets and target classes. Evaluate ASR on globally triggered non-target test images.
baseline_recipes.pass_condition: Pass only if, for each global trigger family, the non-AugMix/non-PixMix poisoned model has ASR_poisoned - ASR_clean > 5 percentage points for at least one target class at exactly <= 1% poison. If no such increase occurs, the attack implementation is too weak to test the robustness claim decisively.
depends_on: Verify that the poisoning budget and global-trigger definitions satisfy the claim before any training
baseline_recipes.rationale: A standard backdoor-poisoning sanity check is to confirm that the same attack succeeds against an unprotected baseline; otherwise low ASR under PixMix or AugMix may be caused by an ineffective attack rather than robustness.
baseline_recipes.label: baseline

baseline_recipes.goal: Directly test the claim on CIFAR-10 for PixMix and AugMix under 1% global-trigger poisoning
baseline_recipes.model: WideResNet-28-10 or ResNet-18; same architecture, optimizer, schedule, and seeds as the clean references
baseline_recipes.method_under_test: PixMix and AugMix training under poisoned versus clean data
baseline_recipes.attack_or_condition: For each method, trigger family, target class, and random seed, train one clean model and one model with exactly <= 1% target-label poisoned training images. Triggers must alter >95% of pixels. Evaluate ASR on all non-target test images with the corresponding global trigger applied.
baseline_recipes.pass_condition: Pass the claim on this dataset only if, for every PixMix and AugMix run, every global trigger family, every target class, and every seed, ASR_poisoned - ASR_clean_same_method_same_seed <= 5 percentage points while poison_fraction <= 1.000% and triggered_pixel_area_fraction > 95.0%. Refute the claim if any compliant poisoned run exceeds its matched clean reference by more than 5 percentage points.
depends_on: Verify that the poisoning budget and global-trigger definitions satisfy the claim before any training
Build clean PixMix and AugMix reference models whose clean-trigger ASR baselines are stable enough for a 5 percentage-point robustness comparison
Validate that the chosen 1% global-trigger poisoning attack is strong enough to measure robustness rather than merely failing by construction
baseline_recipes.rationale: This is the direct matched-budget test required by the claim: same augmentation method, clean versus 1%-poisoned training, global triggers covering more than 95% of image area, and ASR compared to the clean augmented baseline with a 5 percentage-point tolerance.
baseline_recipes.label: baseline

baseline_recipes.goal: Attempt an independent refutation on a second standard vision dataset with the same numeric constraints
baseline_recipes.model: WideResNet-28-10 or ResNet-18; same architecture across clean and poisoned conditions
baseline_recipes.method_under_test: PixMix and AugMix training under poisoned versus clean data
baseline_recipes.attack_or_condition: Repeat the CIFAR-10 headline protocol on CIFAR-100 using target-label global-trigger poisoning at exactly <= 1% of training data. Use the same two trigger families: full-image noise pattern and global intensity/contrast manipulation, each altering >95% of pixels.
baseline_recipes.pass_condition: Pass the claim on this dataset only if, for every PixMix and AugMix run, every trigger family, every target class, and every seed, ASR_poisoned - ASR_clean_same_method_same_seed <= 5 percentage points while poison_fraction <= 1.000% and triggered_pixel_area_fraction > 95.0%. Refute the broad claim if any compliant poisoned run exceeds the matched clean reference by more than 5 percentage points.
depends_on: Verify that the poisoning budget and global-trigger definitions satisfy the claim before any training
Build clean PixMix and AugMix reference models whose clean-trigger ASR baselines are stable enough for a 5 percentage-point robustness comparison
Validate that the chosen 1% global-trigger poisoning attack is strong enough to measure robustness rather than merely failing by construction
Directly test the claim on CIFAR-10 for PixMix and AugMix under 1% global-trigger poisoning
baseline_recipes.rationale: Because the claim is not dataset-specific, a failure on another common classification benchmark is a concrete refutation. CIFAR-100 keeps resolution and training cost similar while changing class granularity.
baseline_recipes.label: baseline

baseline_recipes.goal: Check that headline results are not artifacts of one poison rate, one trigger strength, or a weak/random attack
baseline_recipes.method_under_test: PixMix and AugMix compared with matched non-PixMix/non-AugMix controls
baseline_recipes.attack_or_condition: Run a sweep over poison fractions 0%, 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1.0% for the same >95% area global triggers. Include matched random-label or mismatched-trigger poison controls at 1.0%, plus the non-PixMix/non-AugMix baseline.
baseline_recipes.pass_condition: Pass only if all PixMix and AugMix runs with poison_fraction <= 1.000% and trigger area >95.0% satisfy ASR_poisoned - ASR_clean <= 5 percentage points, and the intentional target-label attack at 1.0% exceeds the random-label or mismatched-trigger poison control by >5 percentage points on the non-PixMix/non-AugMix baseline. Refute the robustness claim if any PixMix or AugMix setting within the claimed budget exceeds the clean reference by more than 5 percentage points.
depends_on: Directly test the claim on CIFAR-10 for PixMix and AugMix under 1% global-trigger poisoning
baseline_recipes.rationale: Attack-strength sweeps and matched random controls are standard checks that the observed ASR is caused by the intended backdoor mechanism and that the claimed robustness is not hiding a failure at a different poison fraction within the allowed up-to-1% budget.
baseline_recipes.label: baseline
